title: InferredArrayElementPositions
description: Issue #166: an array inferred from `items` rather than declared with "type":"array" reduced its element sub-schema to at most the one JSON type that sub-schema declared, and dropped every other keyword beside it -- so {"items":{"type":"object","required":["a"]}} accepted [{}] while the identical sub-schema under "type":"array" rejected it. The same reduction sat on a $ref element, on a prefixItems slot, on the tail `items` governs past a prefix, and on the sub-schema of `contains`. Every position an inferred array can occupy is here, each beside the declared spelling that has always been right, and each beside a non-array instance -- which `items` says nothing about and which must keep being accepted.

prop.$comment: The reported position: an inferred array as a declared property.

propRef.$comment: The same element written as a $ref. The reduction was applied to the *target*, so the arm that calls the named type's Validate was reached only when the target declared no single type -- and this target declares one.

declared.$comment: The accept-control and the contrast the issue is named for: the same element sub-schema under an explicit "type":"array", which rejected [{}] all along and must go on doing so.

inDeclaredArray.$comment: An inferred array as the element of a declared one.

inInferredArray.$comment: An inferred array as the element of another inferred one.

mapValue.$comment: An inferred array as the value of a map.

slotOfDeclared.$comment: The working sibling: a tuple slot of a *declared* array already walked the ladder that materializes a named type, so this rejected [[{}]] before the fix and must not move.

viaRef.$comment: The inferred array reached through a $ref of its own.

allOfBranch.$comment: An inferred array contributed by an allOf branch. The merge types it "array" off the branch's `items` so the merged schema can be typed at all, and that guess was read as a declaration: the Go type became a plain slice, which refused the string, the object, the number and the null this schema all permit.

allOfDeclaringBranch.$comment: The control for the row above, and the one shape that decides which way it reads. A *second* branch declares "type":"array", so the merge is no longer guessing and the plain slice is right -- "str" must be refused here, and accepted one property up. The branches are in this order on purpose: the guess is recorded by the first, and only a rule that keeps looking after it withdraws the guess when the second arrives.

anyOfBranch.$comment: The other two composition spellings are judged by branch matching rather than by a merged type, and were already right. Controls.

ownSlot.$comment: A prefixItems slot of the inferred array itself, which took the reduction rather than the ladder.

ownTail.$comment: Draft 2020-12's `items` beside a prefix is the tail every position past it must satisfy, and it kept only the tail's declared JSON type.

containsShape.$comment: `contains` reduced its sub-schema the same way, to a JSON type and the scalar bounds, so it counted every object and this accepted an array with no matching element.

declaredContains.$comment: The declared spelling of the same keyword. It shares extractContainsDef, so it dropped `required` too -- the one row here where the declared array was no better off than the inferred one.

containsEvaluates.$comment: `contains` is also read by unevaluatedItems, which counts an item contains matched as evaluated. That reader had arms for a const, an enum and the flat checks, so a delegated sub-schema left every item looking unevaluated and this refused the array its own contains had accounted for -- a false rejection introduced by the delegation itself, which is why it is here.

elemMinLength.$comment: An element stating a keyword and no type at all. minLength says nothing about a number, so [7] stays valid.

elemPattern.$comment: An element stating a type *and* a keyword: the reduction kept the type and dropped the pattern.

elemUnion.$comment: An element whose "type" names two JSON kinds. The reduction asks len(type) == 1 and so said nothing at all.

elemNullableObject.$comment: The same shape with null as the second member. The lightweight check names a single JSON kind and refuses every other, so answering "object" for it would refuse the null -- which is why the JSON-type arm is taken only when the type list has one entry.

nullableSlotOfDeclared.$comment: That same reading in the *declared* array's tuple slot, where it was a false rejection rather than a missing check: [null] was refused by a position that permits it.

keptBounds.$comment: The array-level keywords, which the reduction never touched and which must keep rejecting what they always did.

elemTrue.$comment: The two degenerate element sub-schemas. `true` constrains nothing and `false` admits nothing; both already worked and are here so a widening cannot quietly take either.

selfRef.$comment: A recursive element. The delegation has to terminate on the data rather than on the schema, and the type it names is still being generated when the reference is made.
